analysis.evidence: יַהְוֶה אֱלֹהִים is the subject of וַיִּקַּח, and אֶת marks הָאָדָם as its direct object. The next verb, וַיַּנִּחֵהוּ ‘and he placed him’, identifies the garden of Eden as the man's destination.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ and no suffix.

analysis.evidence: In וַיִּקַּח יַהְוֶה אֱלֹהִים אֶת הָאָדָם, יַהְוֶה names the one who takes the man. אֱלֹהִים stands in apposition to the name.
analysis.morphology: Proper noun, singular, without prefix or suffix
analysis.sense: Personal name of the God of Israel

analysis.evidence: יַהְוֶה אֱלֹהִים is the subject of both וַיִּקַּח (“he took”) and וַיַּנִּחֵהוּ (“he placed him”). Both verbs are masculine singular, identifying one actor who takes the man and places him in the garden of Eden.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine plural absolute, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: אֶת introduces הָאָדָם, “the man,” as the definite direct object of וַיִּקַּח, “took.” יַהְוֶה אֱלֹהִים is the subject.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected direct-object particle without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: אֶת marks הָאָדָם as the definite object of וַיִּקַּח, “he took.” The masculine singular suffix in וַיַּנִּחֵהוּ, “he placed him,” refers back to the same man whom God took and placed in the garden of Eden.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular common noun in the absolute state, with prefixed definite article הָ־.

analysis.evidence: יַהְוֶה אֱלֹהִים is the subject of both verbs. He took הָאָדָם, and the suffix ־הוּ refers back to that man. בְגַן עֵדֶן specifies where God placed him.
analysis.morphology: Hiphil wayyiqtol, third-person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ and third-person masculine singular object suffix ־הוּ.
analysis.sense: place, set down in a location

analysis.evidence: In בְגַן עֵדֶן ‘in the garden of Eden’, עֵדֶן completes the construct phrase. The phrase tells where God placed the man, and the following verbs describe his task of cultivating and keeping the garden.
analysis.morphology: Prefixed preposition בְּ ‘in’ + common noun, singular construct, of common gender.

draft.change: Add a place-name word for עֵדֶן alongside the identically pointed noun meaning delight.
draft.definition: Eden is the place where Yahweh God planted a garden.
draft.evidence: Genesis 2:8 locates the garden with the phrase גַּן בְּעֵדֶן, “a garden in Eden.”

analysis.evidence: In בְגַן עֵדֶן, “in the garden of Eden,” עֵדֶן completes the construct phrase and identifies the garden where Yahweh God placed the man. Genesis 2:8 locates that same garden in Eden.
analysis.morphology: Proper noun, singular, absolute, with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Eden, the place where Yahweh God planted a garden.

analysis.evidence: God places the human in the garden of Eden. The paired purpose expressions לְעָבְדָהּ and וּלְשָׁמְרָהּ describe the tasks of cultivating and guarding it.
analysis.morphology: לְ marking purpose + Qal infinitive construct + third-person feminine singular object suffix הּ

analysis.evidence: After God places the man in the garden of Eden, וּלְשָׁמְרָהּ is paired with לְעָבְדָהּ to express his purpose there. The two verbs describe tending the garden and watching over it.
analysis.morphology: Qal infinitive construct with conjunction וּ־, preposition לְ־, and third-person feminine singular object suffix ־ָהּ.
